newsitem.title: GERMANY: 3,000-point level holds firm for German DAX index.
newsitem.headline: 3,000-point level holds firm for German DAX index.

text.p: German shares ended the day on Friday above the magical 3,000-point level, boosted by a 30-month record high for the dollar, but held off further gains by low volumes and cautious market sentiment.

The 30-share IBIS DAX index ended the day at 3,006.87 points, up 10.75 points or 0.36 percent. Earlier the DAX-30 index ended bourse trade at 3,001.37 points, up 8.06 points, off an earlier lifetime high of 3,011.17 points.
The DAX index finally breached the long-targeted 3,000-point threshold in pre-bourse trade.

A strongly positive environment -- fresh records on Wall Street and the dollar's rise above 1.60 marks -- and upward pressure due to the expiry of DAX options triggered the ascent which left dealers jubilant at reaching 3,000 at last.
Dealers had been seeking all week to push the DAX over 3,000 but failed repeatedly despite coming as close as two points to the target on Thursday.
While the level has limited technical implications, it gave the markets a key psychological boost.
Bank stocks led the advance over the session.
"A lot of the new money is going into financials now, especially the foreign money," a trader commented, noting that banks had underperformed last year.
Commerzbank AG ended IBIS trade up 50 pfennigs at 43.90 marks. The share was buoyed by comments on Thursday by its chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen, who said the shares were undervalued.
Deutsche Bank AG ended the day up 35 pfennigs at 78.90 marks, while Dresdner ended up 1.25 marks at 52.55 marks.

Daimler-Benz AG ended up 2.10 marks at 117.10 marks as the market took in its stride news released Thursday of the imminent departure of Mercedes chief Helmut Werner over a disagreement on a management restructure plan.
"This is certainly not a negative for Daimler. Of course Werner is a great man but people will still have a high opinion of Daimler," the Munich trader commented.
Not all traders were euphoric and some were sceptical that the DAX's current rally can continue.
"Of course we are happy to see the 3,000 mark but it doesn't mean the start of anything big," said one Frankfurt dealer, who said a consolidation would inevitably begin soon.
